justification: Nobody's touching this lineup card, and that's the headline: Saquon Barkley's Questionable tag doesn't scare me when the man is the lead story of a Monday Night Football cover shoot against Dallas, and I'm pairing him with my own Eagles DEF for the same primetime moment — that's a package deal, not a risk. Stroud and Woody Marks ride together out of Houston's Sunday slate because I already spent my last dollar making C.J. the headline over Lisa's meme backfield and I am not benching my own narrative a week after I bought it. Allgeier stays at RB1 over RJ Harvey by less than a point of projection, and when it's that close the guy whose bidding war got written up in the tabloid wins the tiebreaker, full stop. Kittle, Jefferson, and Tetairoa round out a board that's camera-ready top to bottom, and Trey Smack keeps the kicker slot looking like it belongs on a roster instead of an afterthought.
forum_post: Harry, baby, you want star power? I'm fielding Saquon Barkley in primetime on Monday night, C.J. Stroud fresh off carrying this roster to a W, and George Kittle doing Kittle things — that's not a lineup, that's a red carpet. Bijan's great, truly, he's having a great season over there, but a great season isn't a moment and I deal exclusively in moments. See you Sunday, and I mean that with love, because losing to you would still be good content.
